classes.qualifier-missing-from-name: the definition adds an identifying attribute the name lacks (normalisation, a vector or component where the name states a scalar, an ion-only population where the name states an element, a reference-relative value, an equivalent-electron count, an averaged form, extra weighting), so the name alone denotes a broader or different quantity
classes.definition-narrower-than-name: the definition restricts applicability to a subset of the objects the name covers (a coil family, an instrument, a plasma regime or surface, a layer)
classes.abstract-parent-as-quantity: the definition declares a parent, umbrella or structural quantity whose population, component, averaging or specialised forms are fixed by more specific instances
classes.unit-does-not-fit-name: the unit's physical dimension contradicts the quantity the name states
classes.agrees: the definition states the same scope the name states

items.name: time
items.description: Temporal measure expressing an elapsed interval or characteristic duration, including the time denominator used to define a physical rate.
items.documentation:
Time is a temporal measure that expresses an elapsed interval or a characteristic duration used to relate physical change to temporal progression.

For a rate formed from a changing physical amount, the temporal denominator enters the defining relation:

$$
\dot{Q} = \frac{\Delta Q}{\Delta t}
$$

where $\dot{Q}$ is the rate of change of the physical amount $Q$, $\Delta Q$ is its change, and $\Delta t$ is the elapsed time over which that change occurs.

At this general scope, the concept includes a reference timescale such as [Alfvén time](name:alfven_time) and the temporal denominator in a throughput rate such as [coolant mass-to-time ratio](name:coolant_mass_flow_rate). It has no intrinsic spatial, species, application, summation, or averaging restriction; those conventions belong to the specific derived quantity.

A time interval or characteristic duration is distinct from the rate that uses it as a denominator: [alfven_time](name:alfven_time) is a duration, whereas [ratio_of_coolant_mass_to_time](name:coolant_mass_flow_rate) is a mass-throughput rate rather than a duration.

items.name: ion_charge_state_particle_flux
items.description: Ion charge-state particle flux is the signed net flow of thermal and nonthermal ions of one species and charge state through an oriented surface per unit actual area and time.
items.documentation:
Ion charge-state particle flux is the signed net number flow through an oriented surface per unit actual surface area and time for one ion species in one ionization charge state. Opposite crossing directions contribute with opposite signs.

For a local surface element, the flux is the directional first moment of the ion velocity distribution:

$$
\Gamma_{s,c} = \int (\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}) f_{s,c}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $\Gamma_{s,c}$ denotes the particle flux, $s$ identifies the ion species, $c$ identifies its charge state, $\mathbf{v}$ is ion velocity, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the chosen surface unit normal, $f_{s,c}$ is the local phase-space number distribution, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

The population includes thermal and nonthermal ions of the selected species and charge state; it is not summed over charge states or restricted to a particular transport mechanism. The quantity counts particles rather than transported charge or energy and is not a surface-integrated particle rate. No particular geometric direction or plasma region is selected.

For the same orientation and spatial averaging, summing over all ionic charge states gives the [ion particle flux](name:ion_particle_flux). The [parallel](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_particle_flux) and [poloidal](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_particle_flux) members select the magnetic-field-aligned and local poloidal projections of the same ion number transport, respectively. The flux-surface-normal member additionally applies flux-surface averaging to the local normal flux.

Sign convention: Positive when the net ion number flow is in the direction of the chosen surface normal.

items.name: neutral_internal_state_source_rate
items.description: Neutral internal-state source rate is the flux-surface-averaged net particle gain or loss per volume in one specified internal state of a neutral species.
items.documentation:
Neutral internal-state source rate is the flux-surface-averaged volumetric rate at which particles enter or leave one specified internal state of a neutral species. It supplies the source term in the particle-number density transport equation for that state.

The net source rate is defined by

$$
S_{0,a}(\psi)=\left\langle S_{0,a}^{\mathrm{gain}}-S_{0,a}^{\mathrm{loss}}\right\rangle_{\psi}
$$

where $S_{0,a}$ is the neutral internal-state source rate, $S_{0,a}^{\mathrm{gain}}$ and $S_{0,a}^{\mathrm{loss}}$ are the local particle addition and removal rates per volume for the included processes, $0$ denotes electrical neutrality, $a$ identifies the internal state, $\psi$ labels a magnetic flux surface, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\psi}$ denotes a flux-surface average.

This quantity applies to one neutral species and one specified internal state; it is not summed over internal states and excludes charged-particle populations. Internal-state resolution distinguishes populations within the electrically neutral species, not different ionic charge states. The source rate is not the full time derivative of the state density, because spatial transport also changes that density.

Summing these rates over a complete set of internal states, for the same included processes, gives the [neutral source rate](name:neutral_source_rate). Transfers solely between internal states cancel in that sum, although they contribute gains and losses to individual state equations.

Sign convention: Positive when the included processes produce a net gain of particles in the specified neutral internal state; negative values indicate net removal.

items.name: counter_passing_current_density
items.description: Current density is the vector flux density of conventional electric charge, equal to electric current per unit area normal to the flow.
items.documentation:
Current density $\mathbf{J}$ is the vector density of conventional electric-charge flux at a point. It represents the signed flow of electric charge carried by charged particles, with direction defined by positive charge transport.

A kinetic definition is the charge-weighted first velocity moment of the particle distribution functions:

$$
\mathbf{J}(\mathbf{x},t) = \sum_s q_s \int \mathbf{v}\, f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\, d^3v
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $t$ is time, $s$ indexes charged species, $q_s$ is the species charge, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_s$ is the velocity-space distribution function, and $d^3v$ denotes integration over velocity space.

Unless a narrower restriction is specified, the sum includes all charged-particle contributions. In quasistatic equilibrium, current density is the source in Ampere's law, $\nabla \times \mathbf{B} = \mu_0\mathbf{J}$ when displacement current is neglected, and steady charge conservation gives $\nabla \cdot \mathbf{J}=0$. It is distinct from scalar electric current, which is the flux of $\mathbf{J}$ through a specified surface. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, geometric projections include [toroidal current density](name:toroidal_current_density); orbit-restricted forms such as [toroidal counter-passing current density](name:toroidal_counter_passing_current_density) remain instances of this quantity. The parent [current density](name:current_density) excludes displacement-current density.

Sign convention: Positive when the stated component or scalar projection of $\mathbf{J}$ is aligned with the positive direction of the basis vector or unit vector defining that component or projection.

items.name: vertical_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description: Signed vertical component of the pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic fluid velocity for one ion charge state in the edge plasma, distinct from individual guiding-center motion.
items.documentation:
The vertical ion charge-state diamagnetic-drift velocity is the signed projection of the pressure-gradient-driven fluid velocity onto the direction parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis. It applies to one ion charge state in the edge plasma and represents a fluid-moment contribution rather than individual guiding-center motion.

For a specified ion charge state, the defining projection is:

$$
v_{\ast\alpha,Z} = \left(-\frac{\nabla p_\alpha \times \mathbf{B}}{q_\alpha n_\alpha B^2}\right)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $\alpha$ identifies the ion species and charge state, $v_{\ast\alpha,Z}$ is its vertical diamagnetic-drift velocity, $p_\alpha$ is its partial pressure, $\nabla p_\alpha$ is its pressure gradient, $q_\alpha$ is its signed particle charge, $n_\alpha$ is its number density, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector, and $B=|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude. The unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ points along increasing vertical height $Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $\phi$ is toroidal angle.

This quantity is local and charge-state resolved; it is neither summed nor averaged over charge states. In contrast, the [binormal ion velocity due to diamagnetic drift](name:binormal_ion_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) uses a local binormal projection and a density-weighted mean over ionic charge states.

Only the diamagnetic contribution is included; electric-field drift, polarization drift, curvature drift, and independent parallel flow are excluded. The diamagnetic velocity vector is perpendicular to the magnetic field, but its vertical component need not vanish because the vertical direction is not generally field aligned.

Sign convention: Positive when the diamagnetic fluid velocity has a component toward increasing vertical height $Z$.

items.name: radial_coordinate
items.description: Major-radius coordinate of a geometric point or reference position, equal to its perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis.
items.documentation:
Major-radius coordinate of a geometric point or reference position is its perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. Here $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The coordinate is defined by

$$
R = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}
$$

where $x$ and $y$ are the horizontal coordinates of the same point in the right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$ frame, with $z$ the vertical coordinate along the same axis as $Z$.

This coordinate applies to plasma positions and device geometry. It is nonnegative and vanishes on the toroidal symmetry axis; it is distinct from a minor-radius distance measured from the magnetic axis and from a magnetic flux label. No summation, averaging, or weighting is implied by the general coordinate; specialized quantities define their reference positions or aggregation conventions.

For example, the [radial coordinate of a conductor cross-section](name:radial_coordinate_of_conductor_cross_section) locates its geometric center, whereas the [radial coordinate of the current center](name:radial_coordinate_of_current_center) is the toroidal-current-weighted mean major radius over the plasma cross-section.

items.name: vertical_ion_momentum_diffusivity
items.description: Effective coefficient governing down-gradient transport of the total ion population’s vertical momentum along the vertical Z direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The vertical ion momentum diffusivity $D_Z^i$ is the effective coefficient characterizing down-gradient redistribution of the vertical component of momentum within the total ion population summed over all charge states. It is the vertical-direction component of [ion momentum diffusivity] in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The vertical diffusive momentum-flux density is defined by:

$$
\Gamma_{\mathrm{mom},i}^{ZZ} = -\rho_i D_Z^i \frac{\partial v_{i,Z}}{\partial Z}
$$

where $\Gamma_{\mathrm{mom},i}^{ZZ}$ is the flux density of vertical ion momentum in the vertical direction, $\rho_i$ is total ion mass density in kg m$^{-3}$, $v_{i,Z}$ is the mass-weighted mean vertical ion-fluid velocity in m s$^{-1}$, and $Z$ is vertical height in m. The minus sign makes the diffusive flux oppose the vertical velocity gradient.

This coefficient is charge-state summed and is distinct from [vertical ion charge state momentum diffusivity](name:vertical_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusivity), which resolves one ion charge state. Its cylindrical vertical direction also distinguishes it from the poloidal transport represented by [poloidal ion momentum diffusivity](name:poloidal_ion_momentum_diffusivity).

items.name: parallel_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusivity
items.description: Fickian coefficient relating density-normalized diffusive heat flux of a neutral species in one internal state to its temperature gradient along the local magnetic field.
items.documentation:
The parallel neutral internal-state energy diffusivity characterizes gradient-driven transport of thermal energy carried by one neutral species in one specified internal state. It describes only the contribution along the local magnetic field, not the full thermal-energy flux.

The defining relation for the density-normalized parallel diffusive heat flux is:

$$
\frac{Q_{0,a,\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff}}}{n_{0,a}} = -D_{0,a,W,\parallel}\,\hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\nabla T_{0,a}
$$

where $Q_{0,a,\parallel}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the field-parallel diffusive thermal-energy flux, $n_{0,a}$ is the number density of the selected neutral population, $T_{0,a}$ is its temperature expressed as thermal energy, and $D_{0,a,W,\parallel}$ is this diffusivity. The index $0$ denotes neutral particles, $a$ identifies their internal state, and $W$ denotes the energy transport channel. The unit vector $\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf B/|\mathbf B|$ follows the local magnetic field $\mathbf B$, and $\nabla$ denotes the spatial gradient. The minus sign specifies down-gradient transport for a nonnegative diffusivity.

This coefficient applies to the selected species and internal state without summing or averaging over species or states. It excludes convective and advective heat transport and does not specify perpendicular diffusion. The magnetic field defines the projection direction; it does not imply magnetic confinement of neutrals.

Relative to the broader [neutral energy diffusion coefficient](name:neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient), this quantity resolves both an internal state and the field-parallel transport direction. The analogous [parallel ion charge-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient) instead applies to ions in a specified charge state.

items.name: radiated_power_density
items.description: Power density due to radiation is the local volumetric rate at which plasma energy is converted into emitted electromagnetic radiation.
items.documentation:
Power density due to radiation is the local volumetric rate at which plasma energy is converted into emitted electromagnetic radiation. It is the non-negative magnitude of radiative energy loss from the emitting plasma volume.

The radiated power density is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{rad}} = \frac{\mathrm{d}P_{\mathrm{emit}}}{\mathrm{d}V}
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{emit}}$ is the emitted electromagnetic power and $V$ is the emitting volume. This quantity represents radiative emission rather than the signed source term in the plasma energy balance; radiation contributes negatively to that balance. It is a volumetric quantity and is distinct from the incident surface flux represented by flux at wall due to radiation. The broader [power density] includes radiative and non-radiative source or loss mechanisms.

items.name: particle_source_rate_due_to_distribution_function_driven
items.description: Distribution-function-driven particle source rate is the net particle gain or loss per physical volume and time contributed by a kinetic source to a specified population.
items.documentation:
Distribution-function-driven particle source rate describes the contribution of a specified kinetic source to the particle balance of a plasma population. It counts particles added or removed, rather than the energy or momentum transferred to them.

The volumetric rate is the velocity-space integral of the distribution-function source term:

$$
S(\mathbf{x},t)=\int Q(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v
$$

where $S$ is the volumetric particle source rate, $Q$ is the source term in the population's distribution-function equation, $\mathbf{x}$ is physical position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $t$ is time, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The integral covers all particle velocities.

The quantity includes only the specified kinetic-source contribution, not all contributions to the population's particle balance. It imposes no particular species, charge-state, or thermal-population restriction. It is velocity-integrated, not a phase-space-resolved source density; no spatial averaging is implied.

Integrating this rate over a specified physical volume gives the [volume-integrated particle source rate](name:volume_integrated_particle_source_rate) for the same population and source contribution.

Sign convention: Positive when the source adds particles to the specified population; negative when it removes particles.

items.name: electron_density
items.description: Number density of electrons is the local number of plasma electrons per physical volume.
items.documentation:
Number density of electron

The local density is the differential electron count per physical volume:

$$
n_e(\mathbf{x},t) = \frac{dN_e}{dV}
$$

where $n_e$ is electron number density, $\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position, $t$ is time, $N_e$ is the number of plasma electrons in the local volume, and $V$ is physical volume.

This quantity applies to plasma electrons at a local position and does not specify a particular plasma region or spatial average. It does not itself select a thermal, fast, or orbit-class population; its aggregation is local rather than line- or volume-averaged.

It counts particles rather than weighting them by electric charge, and is distinct from an electron inventory integrated over a region. [Thermal electron density](name:thermal_electron_density) and [fast electron density](name:fast_electron_density) select particular electron populations, while [total electron density](name:total_electron_density) denotes the complete included electron population.

[Line-averaged electron density](name:line_averaged_electron_density) is an average of local electron density along a path, and [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density) is its average over a volume.

items.name: plasma_energy
items.description: Plasma energy is the volume-integrated internal kinetic energy carried by all confined electron and ion populations, including thermal and suprathermal particles. It excludes electromagnetic-field, rest-mass, and organized bulk-flow energy.
items.documentation:
Plasma energy is the volume-integrated internal kinetic energy carried by all confined electron and ion populations, including thermal and suprathermal populations. It is the all-population stored particle energy of the confined plasma, not a thermal-only component.

A pressure-tensor definition gives the stored particle energy without assuming isotropic distributions:

$$
W_\mathrm{p} = \int_{V_\mathrm{p}} \sum_a \frac{1}{2}\,\operatorname{Tr}\mathbf{P}_a\, dV
$$

where $W_\mathrm{p}$ is the plasma energy, $V_\mathrm{p}$ is the confined plasma volume, $a$ labels the electron, ion, and modeled suprathermal populations included in the confined plasma, $\mathbf{P}_a$ is the pressure tensor of population $a$ in its local mean-flow frame, and $dV$ is the scalar volume element. For isotropic populations this reduces to the pressure-sum relation with energy density $3p_\mathrm{tot}/2$, where $p_\mathrm{tot}=\sum_a p_a$; for a gyrotropic anisotropic population the contribution is $p_{\perp a}+p_{\parallel a}/2$.

This quantity excludes electromagnetic-field energy, electrostatic-field energy, rest-mass energy, and organized macroscopic bulk-flow energy. [Electron energy](name:volume_integrated_square_of_poloidal_magnetic_field), [thermal plasma energy](name:thermal_plasma_energy), and [fast-particle energy](name:fast_particle_energy) are component contributions, while total plasma energy and total particle energy denote the corresponding all-population stored particle-energy concept when the naming emphasizes totality.

items.name: absorbed_wave_power
items.description: Net electromagnetic-wave power transferred directly from coherent waves to a selected plasma particle population, integrated over the plasma volume and resolved by species or charge state.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the net rate at which coherent electromagnetic waves transfer energy directly to selected plasma particles. The selected population may be electrons, ions, or a specified ion charge state, with the result integrated over the plasma volume.

$$
P_{\rm abs} = \left.\frac{dE_{\rm particles}}{dt}\right|_{\rm waves}
$$

where $P_{\rm abs}$ is absorbed wave power, $E_{\rm particles}$ is the energy of the selected particle population, and the subscript “waves” restricts the energy-transfer rate to direct coupling from the electromagnetic wave field. This is the absorbed component of [wave power](name:wave_power), distinct from electromagnetic power that remains carried by the wave.

The quantity includes direct wave-to-particle transfer and excludes subsequent collisional redistribution between particle populations. Species-resolved and charge-state-resolved instances include [electron absorbed wave power](name:thermal_electron_absorbed_power) and ion charge-state absorbed wave power.

items.name: total_ion_particle_volumetric_source_rate
items.description: Total ion particle volumetric source rate is the net local ion addition or removal per physical volume, summed over all ion species and ionic charge states.
items.documentation:
Total ion particle volumetric source rate is the net local rate of ion addition or removal per physical volume, summed over all ion species and ionic charge states. It supplies the source contribution to the total ion number-density balance through ionization, recombination, and particle exchange processes.

For a specified source contribution, the net rate is defined by

$$
S_i = \sum_a \sum_{z\geq 1}\left(S_{a,z,\mathrm{in}}-S_{a,z,\mathrm{out}}\right)
$$

where $S_i$ is the total ion particle volumetric source rate, $a$ indexes ion species, $z$ is the positive ionic charge number, and $S_{a,z,\mathrm{in}}$ and $S_{a,z,\mathrm{out}}$ are the local rates per physical volume of particles entering and leaving the corresponding ionic state.

The aggregation is over ion species and ionic charge states, not necessarily over separate source contributions. Each ion is counted once, without charge weighting; neutral particles and electrons are excluded. Transfers between included ionic states cancel in the sum when they conserve ion number. This source term is distinct from the full time derivative of ion density, which also includes particle transport.

Integrating this volumetric rate over a specified plasma volume gives the [total ion particle source rate](name:total_ion_particle_source_rate). Integrating over the volume enclosed by a magnetic flux surface gives the [cumulative total ion particle source rate inside that surface](name:cumulative_inside_flux_surface_total_ion_particle_source_rate).

Sign convention: Positive when the specified source produces a net gain of ions; negative values indicate net removal.

items.name: flux_surface_averaged_current_density_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive
items.description: Vector average on a magnetic flux surface of conventional plasma current density generated non-inductively by electromagnetic-wave–particle interactions, excluding inductive and non-wave current drive.
items.documentation:
Flux-surface-averaged wave-driven current density is the vector average, on a magnetic flux surface, of the conventional plasma current density generated non-inductively by electromagnetic-wave–particle interactions. It retains the vector character of the local current-density contribution while averaging its resolved components over the surface.

The flux-surface average is defined componentwise by

$$
\left\langle \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{wd}} \right\rangle_{\psi}
=
\frac{\displaystyle\int_{S_{\psi}} \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{wd}}\,\frac{dS}{\lvert\nabla\psi\rvert}}
{\displaystyle\int_{S_{\psi}}\frac{dS}{\lvert\nabla\psi\rvert}}
$$

where $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{wd}}$ is the local conventional current-density vector generated by wave–particle interactions, $\psi$ is the scalar magnetic-flux label, $S_{\psi}$ is the corresponding magnetic flux surface, $dS$ is its surface-area element, and $\nabla\psi$ is the spatial gradient of the flux label.

The quantity applies to the plasma current on one magnetic flux surface and includes the wave-driven contributions of the charged-particle populations represented in the conventional current. Its aggregation convention is a complete flux-surface average, not a local value, volume average, toroidal current integral, or Fourier-mode-resolved contribution.

It excludes inductive current density and current contributions generated by bootstrap, ohmic, or other non-wave current-drive mechanisms. No field-aligned or other directional projection is imposed at this parent level.

This quantity is obtained by applying flux-surface averaging to the local [wave-driven current density](name:current_density_due_to_wave_driven_current_drive). The parallel flux-surface-averaged wave-driven current density is a specialization that retains only the component projected along the magnetic-field direction before or within the averaging operation.

Sign convention: Positive when a resolved current-density component points in the corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ basis, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, consistent with conventional positive-charge transport.

items.name: power_due_to_electron_cyclotron_heating
items.description: Net radiofrequency power absorbed by the plasma through electron cyclotron heating, with source aggregation determined by scope and excluding launched or reflected power.
items.documentation:
Electron-cyclotron heating power is the rate at which electron-cyclotron-range electromagnetic waves transfer energy to the plasma, principally through resonant electron absorption. It denotes deposited plasma heating power rather than generator, launched, transmitted, or reflected power.

The absorbed power is defined by the volume integral of the local electron-cyclotron heating density:

$$
P_{\mathrm{EC}} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{plasma}}} Q_{\mathrm{EC}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{EC}}$ is the absorbed power, $Q_{\mathrm{EC}}$ is the local power-transfer density, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, and $V_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the plasma volume. Source aggregation is scope-dependent; the [total electron-cyclotron heating power](name:total_power_due_to_electron_cyclotron_heating) sums the contributions from all electron-cyclotron wave sources. The quantity is non-negative for net absorption and is distinct from [electron absorbed wave power](name:thermal_electron_absorbed_power) when that quantity includes wave absorption without restricting the mechanism to electron cyclotron heating.

items.name: gap_at_closest_wall_point
items.description: Gap at closest wall point is the minimum geometric clearance between the plasma separatrix and the nearest limiter or wall element.
items.documentation:
Gap at closest wall point

The gap is defined by

$$
g = \min_{\mathbf{x}\in\Gamma_{\mathrm{sep}},\,\mathbf{y}\in\Gamma_{\mathrm{pw}}} \left\|\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{y}\right\|_2
$$

where $g$ is the gap, $\Gamma_{\mathrm{sep}}$ is the set of points on the plasma separatrix, $\Gamma_{\mathrm{pw}}$ is the combined set of points on the limiter or wall boundary, $\mathbf{x}$ and $\mathbf{y}$ are physical positions on those respective boundaries, and $\left\|\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{y}\right\|_2$ is their Euclidean distance.

The quantity applies to the plasma separatrix and the limiter or wall boundary. Its aggregation is the minimum over all separatrix-point and material-boundary-point pairs.

This is a geometric clearance, not a radial coordinate, a distance to an arbitrarily selected wall point, or an average over the wall. It is distinct from the [gap at the outboard midplane](name:gap_at_outboard_midplane), which is the major-radius separation between inner and outer separatrices in a double-null or near-double-null equilibrium.

For the same separatrix and limiter or wall boundary, this quantity is the same minimum-clearance quantity as the [gap at the plasma boundary](name:gap_at_plasma_boundary).

items.name: electron_power_density
items.description: Electron power density is the net rate at which energy is transferred to or from the electron population per unit volume. It is the scalar source term for the electron recipient in an electron energy balance, including applicable source and sink channels.
items.documentation:
Electron power density is the net rate at which energy is transferred to or from the electron population per unit volume. It is the scalar source term for the electron recipient in an electron energy transport equation, including only the source and sink terms assigned to electrons in that balance.

For a differential volume, the electron power density is defined by

$$
p_e = \frac{dE_e}{dt\,dV}
$$

where $p_e$ is the electron power density, $E_e$ is the signed energy transfer to the electron population through the included electron energy source and sink channels, $t$ is time, and $V$ is physical volume.

The scope is the electron population in the specified plasma region, with contributions from applicable heating, collisional energy exchange, ionization, recombination, radiation loss, and other electron energy-transfer processes when those terms are assigned to the electron balance. The aggregation convention is a net local source term over the included electron channels; it is not an individual process contribution, a diagnostic-specific estimate, a flux-surface average, or a total stored electron energy.

Electron power density specializes power density to the electron recipient. It excludes source terms whose recipient is another population, such as [ion power density](name:ion_power_density) or [neutral power density](name:neutral_power_density), even when the same interaction exchanges energy between populations; it is also distinct from radiated power density, which represents energy emitted as radiation rather than the net source assigned to the electron recipient.

The volume integral of $p_e$ over a specified plasma region gives [electron power](name:volume_integrated_electron_power_density) for the same electron energy balance. When recipient-resolved source terms are defined for the same region and channel set, their aggregate contributes to net plasma power density.

Sign convention: Positive when the included balance terms increase the energy of the electron population.

items.name: radial_total_ion_energy_flux
items.description: Total ion energy flux across magnetic flux surfaces is the net outward energy transport per unit area, averaged over each surface and summed over all ion species and charge states.
items.documentation:
Total ion energy flux across magnetic flux surfaces represents the surface-averaged transport of energy carried by the aggregate ion population. It includes conductive thermal-energy transport and convective enthalpy or bulk-kinetic transport.

The defining surface average is:

$$
\Gamma_{i,W}^{\mathrm{out}} = \frac{\int_S \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{i,W}^{\mathrm{tot}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}\,dA}{\int_S dA}
$$

where $\Gamma_{i,W}^{\mathrm{out}}$ is the surface-averaged outward ion energy flux, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{i,W}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the [total ion energy-flux vector](name:total_ion_energy_flux), $S$ is the magnetic flux surface, $\hat{\mathbf n}$ is its outward unit normal, and $dA$ is a surface-area element. The subscripts $i$ and $W$ identify the ion population and energy channel, respectively.

The aggregation is a sum over all ion species and charge states, not a density-weighted mean. The [ion charge-state energy flux](name:ion_charge_state_energy_flux) instead restricts transport to one specified charge state. Electron and neutral energy transport are excluded. Surface averaging preserves a flux density; integrating the normal flux over the surface instead gives the energy-transfer rate through that surface.

The magnetic-surface-normal projection is distinct from the major-radius projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

Sign convention: Positive when net ion energy transport is outward through the magnetic flux surface, toward increasing enclosed volume.

items.name: perpendicular_fast_electron_pressure
items.description: Pressure of fast electrons perpendicular to the local magnetic field is the mean transverse normal stress produced by random suprathermal electron motion.
items.documentation:
Pressure of fast electrons perpendicular to the local magnetic field is the mean of the two transverse normal stresses carried by the suprathermal electron population. For a gyrotropic population, these two stresses are equal.

The perpendicular pressure $p_{e,\mathrm{f},\perp}$ is defined by

$$
p_{e,\mathrm{f},\perp}=\frac{1}{2}\left[\operatorname{tr}\mathbf{P}_{e,\mathrm{f}}-\hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\mathbf{P}_{e,\mathrm{f}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}\right]
$$

where $\mathbf{P}_{e,\mathrm{f}}$ is the [fast-electron pressure tensor](name:fast_electron_pressure), describing momentum transport from electron motion relative to the fast-electron population's mean velocity; $\operatorname{tr}$ denotes the tensor trace; and $\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf B/|\mathbf B|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field $\mathbf B$. The subscript $\mathrm{f}$ identifies the fast population.

This local quantity includes the fast-electron population without a trapped- or passing-orbit restriction. The transverse stresses are averaged, not summed. It excludes thermal-electron pressure, ion pressure, and momentum flux associated with the population's mean flow; it does not select only electrons whose velocities are entirely perpendicular to the field.

The complementary field-aligned contraction is the [parallel fast-electron pressure](name:parallel_fast_electron_pressure). Together, the perpendicular and parallel pressures determine the gyrotropic fast-electron pressure tensor; they coincide in the isotropic limit.

items.name: poloidal_neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description: Dimensionless coefficient setting the free-streaming upper bound on the flux of poloidal momentum carried by a neutral species, limiting flux magnitude without reversing its sign.
items.documentation:
The poloidal neutral momentum flux-limiter coefficient bounds transport of the poloidal component of neutral-particle [momentum](name:momentum) in fluid transport closures. It is the poloidal component of the [neutral momentum flux-limiter coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), applied to a selected neutral species.

The limiting flux magnitude is defined by:

$$
\Pi_{0,\mathrm{p}}^{\max} = \alpha_{0,\mathrm{p}}\,\Pi_{0,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $\alpha_{0,\mathrm{p}}$ is this coefficient, $\Pi_{0,\mathrm{p}}^{\max}$ is the permitted upper bound on momentum-flux magnitude, and $\Pi_{0,\mathrm{p}}^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the corresponding free-streaming reference magnitude. The subscript $0$ identifies the neutral species, and $\mathrm{p}$ identifies its poloidal momentum component.

The flux describes momentum crossing an oriented surface. The poloidal label selects the transported momentum component, not the direction normal to that surface. Limiting constrains the flux magnitude while preserving its sign; the coefficient is neither the momentum flux itself nor a momentum diffusivity.

This coefficient applies at the neutral-species level without selecting an internal state. The [poloidal neutral-state momentum flux-limiter coefficient](name:poloidal_neutral_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) instead applies to a specified neutral state; the species-level coefficient is not defined as a sum of state-resolved coefficients.

items.name: radial_ion_energy_convection_velocity
items.description: Effective radial transport velocity for convective ion-energy transport in the edge plasma; it need not equal the radial ion particle-flow velocity.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the effective velocity assigned to the convective component of ion-energy transport in the edge plasma. It parameterizes energy advection and is not, by definition, the ion particle-flow velocity.

Its defining relation to the convective ion-energy flux is

$$
u_{i,E,r}^{\mathrm{conv}} = \frac{Q_{i,E,r}^{\mathrm{conv}}}{W_{i,E}}$$

where $Q_{i,E,r}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the radial convective ion-energy flux and $W_{i,E}$ is the corresponding ion-energy density. The quantity is defined where $W_{i,E}$ is nonzero and excludes diffusive, conductive, and source contributions. It is the radial component of ion_energy_convection_velocity, and differs from [radial_ion_convection_velocity](name:radial_ion_particle_convection_velocity), which parameterizes particle transport.

Sign convention: Positive when the associated convective ion-energy flux points in the $+\hat{R}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: toroidal_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description: Dimensionless coefficient that scales the collisionless free-streaming upper bound on toroidal momentum-flux density in multi-fluid edge plasma transport closures, capping the flux magnitude while leaving its sign direction unchanged.
items.documentation:
In multi-fluid edge plasma transport models, gradient-driven diffusive closures can produce toroidal momentum-flux densities that exceed the physically realizable collisionless free-streaming limit in steep-gradient regions. A toroidal momentum-flux-limiter coefficient $\alpha_{m,\phi}$ is introduced to bound the effective $\hat{\phi}$-projected momentum-flux density, where $m$ denotes momentum and $\phi$ denotes the toroidal projection. The toroidal projection is along $\hat{\phi}$, the tangent to increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$ and $\hat{R} \times \hat{\phi} = \hat{Z}$.

The bounded toroidal momentum-flux density satisfies the limiter constraint:

$$
|\Pi_{\phi}^{\mathrm{lim}}| \le \alpha_{m,\phi}\,\Pi_{\phi}^{\mathrm{FS}}
$$

where $\Pi_{\phi}^{\mathrm{lim}}$ is the limited toroidal momentum-flux density, $\Pi_{\phi}^{\mathrm{FS}}$ is the toroidal free-streaming momentum-flux reference scale, and $\alpha_{m,\phi}$ is the toroidal momentum-flux-limiter coefficient.

This coefficient is the toroidal directional specialization of [momentum-flux-limiter coefficient](name:momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), not a particle-, heat-, or energy-flux limiter and not the momentum-flux density itself. It is intrinsically non-negative: it caps the magnitude of the modeled toroidal momentum-flux density and does not carry the positive or negative sign of that flux. Directional siblings include the poloidal, radial, [parallel](name:parallel_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), and [diamagnetic] momentum-flux-limiter coefficients.

items.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
items.description: Projection along the local magnetic field of the E×B guiding-center drift for one ion charge state in the edge plasma, identically zero for the ideal drift.
items.documentation:
The parallel component of the [ion charge-state E×B drift velocity](name:ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) is its signed projection along the local magnetic-field direction.

For the ideal E×B drift, the defining projection is

$$
v_{E,\parallel} = \mathbf{v}_E \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}} = \frac{(\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B})\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}}{|\mathbf{B}|^2} = 0.
$$

Here $v_{E,\parallel}$ is the parallel drift component for the specified ion charge state, $\mathbf{v}_E$ is its E×B guiding-center drift velocity, $\mathbf{E}$ is the local electric field, $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic field, $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector directed along the magnetic field. The definition requires a nonzero magnetic field.

This quantity applies locally to one specified charge state of one ion species in the magnetized edge plasma; it is neither summed nor averaged over charge states or species. The ideal E×B drift is independent of ion mass and charge for fixed local fields. This component does not denote the total parallel ion velocity, and contributions from other mechanisms are excluded.

Unlike the [toroidal component](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift), which need not vanish, the field-aligned component vanishes identically because the ideal E×B drift is perpendicular to the local magnetic field.

items.name: poloidal_linear_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux
items.description: Poloidal linear-momentum flux is the signed transfer of poloidal momentum per unit area and time carried by neutral particles of one species in one specified internal state across an oriented surface.
items.documentation:
Poloidal linear-momentum flux is the signed rate per unit area at which the poloidal component of [momentum](name:momentum), carried by a specified neutral species in one internal state, crosses an oriented surface. It is the poloidal projection of the state-resolved momentum transport, not an angular-momentum flux.

For a surface with chosen unit normal $\hat{\mathbf n}$, the defining projection is:

$$
\Gamma_{0,a,\mathrm p}(\hat{\mathbf n}) = \hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm p}\cdot\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{0,a}(\hat{\mathbf n})
$$

where $\Gamma_{0,a,\mathrm p}$ is this poloidal flux, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{0,a}$ is the vector-valued [linear neutral internal-state momentum flux](name:linear_neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux) across the same surface, and $\hat{\mathbf e}_{\mathrm p}$ is the positive poloidal unit tangent. The subscript $0$ denotes neutral particles, $a$ labels their specified internal state, and $\mathrm p$ denotes the poloidal projection.

The poloidal tangent lies on a magnetic flux surface toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, where $\rho$ labels flux surfaces and $\phi$ is the toroidal angle. The associated right-handed cylindrical frame is $(R,\phi,Z)$, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height. The poloidal projection specifies the transported momentum component; it does not prescribe a radial or flux-surface-normal crossing direction.

The quantity includes the convective and stress contributions of the selected neutral state, rather than only a diffusive contribution. It excludes other internal states, other species, particle-number flux, and local momentum sources. Summing over all internal states of the same neutral species gives the [poloidal neutral momentum flux](name:poloidal_neutral_momentum_flux) across the same oriented surface; no internal-state sum is implicit here.

Sign convention: Positive when the signed transfer across the surface along $\hat{\mathbf n}$ has a net momentum component toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

items.name: normalized_toroidal_beta
items.description: Normalized toroidal beta is the whole-plasma toroidal pressure-to-reference-magnetic-pressure ratio scaled by plasma minor radius and reference toroidal field relative to plasma current, with a defining factor of 100.
items.documentation:
Normalized toroidal beta is the whole-plasma toroidal pressure-to-reference-magnetic-pressure ratio further normalized by plasma size, reference toroidal field, and plasma current.

The defining normalization is:

$$\beta = \frac{2\mu_0 \langle p\rangle}{B^2}$$

Here $\beta_{\mathrm{N}}$ is normalized toroidal beta, $\beta_{\mathrm{t}}$ is [toroidal beta](name:toroidal_beta), $a$ is plasma minor radius, $B_0$ is the reference toroidal magnetic-field magnitude, and $I_p$ is total plasma current. The factor 100 and the prescribed numerical normalization of the dimensional factors are part of the definition. The toroidal pressure ratio is $\beta_{\mathrm{t}} = 2\mu_0\langle p\rangle/B_0^2$, where $\mu_0$ is vacuum permeability and $\langle p\rangle$ is volume-averaged plasma pressure.

This is a global whole-plasma quantity: its pressure is volume-averaged rather than evaluated at a point. The pressure population follows the corresponding toroidal beta; the normalization does not convert a thermal-pressure input to total pressure or vice versa. It is therefore distinct from a local or pedestal beta, and from unnormalized toroidal beta by its additional size, reference-field, and current factors.

For the same pressure and consistent magnetic-field scales, [plasma beta](name:beta), [poloidal beta](name:poloidal_beta), and [toroidal beta](name:toroidal_beta) satisfy $1/\beta = 1/\beta_{\mathrm{p}} + 1/\beta_{\mathrm{t}}$, where $\beta$ is plasma beta and $\beta_{\mathrm{p}}$ is poloidal beta. Normalized toroidal beta rescales $\beta_{\mathrm{t}}$ and does not replace it in this relationship.

items.name: toroidal_ion_momentum_convection_velocity
items.description: Effective velocity coefficient multiplying one ion species' toroidal momentum density to give its convective flux across magnetic flux surfaces.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the effective convection coefficient for cross-flux-surface transport of the toroidal component of [momentum](name:momentum) carried by one ion species. It is a transport-closure coefficient, distinct from the species' toroidal bulk-flow velocity.

The convective momentum flux is defined by:

$$
\Pi_{i,\phi}^{\mathrm{conv}} = V_{i,\phi}^{\mathrm{conv}} p_{i,\phi}
$$

where $\Pi_{i,\phi}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the outward-directed convective flux of toroidal momentum, $V_{i,\phi}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is this effective convection coefficient, $p_{i,\phi}$ is the toroidal linear momentum density, and $i$ identifies the ion species. The toroidal angle $\phi$ belongs to the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from the symmetry axis and $Z$ is vertical height.

The coefficient applies to one ion species, with its transported momentum summed over all ionic charge states, not over different ion species. The [charge-state-resolved coefficient](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity) instead applies to one specified charge state. Gradient-driven diffusion and residual stress are separate momentum-flux contributions.

This quantity specializes [ion momentum convection velocity](name:ion_momentum_convection_velocity) to transport of toroidal momentum: the toroidal label identifies the transported momentum component, not the direction of convection. The sign of the convective momentum flux depends on both the coefficient and the transported momentum density.

Sign convention: Positive when the effective convection is directed outward toward the last closed flux surface; negative when directed inward toward the magnetic axis. Toroidal momentum is positive in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field
items.description: Complex E-minus contribution of a coherent electromagnetic-wave electric field, transverse to the static magnetic field and retaining the amplitude and phase of its right-hand circular polarization.
items.documentation:
The right-hand circularly polarized wave electric field is the E-minus polarization contribution of the complex [wave electric field](name:wave_electric_field), perpendicular to the local static magnetic field. It retains the local amplitude and phase of that circular-polarization contribution.

Its vector contribution is defined by the circular-basis projection

$$
\widetilde{\mathbf E}_{-}=\widetilde E_{-}\mathbf e_{-}=\mathbf e_{-}\left(\mathbf e_{-}^{*}\cdot\widetilde{\mathbf E}_{\mathrm{wave}}\right)
$$

where $\widetilde{\mathbf E}_{-}$ is the right-hand circularly polarized vector contribution, $\widetilde E_{-}$ is its complex coefficient, $\widetilde{\mathbf E}_{\mathrm{wave}}$ is the wave-electric-field phasor, and the asterisk denotes complex conjugation. The circular basis vector is $\mathbf e_{-}=(\hat{\mathbf e}_1+i\hat{\mathbf e}_2)/\sqrt{2}$, where $i$ is the imaginary unit. The real unit vectors form a local right-handed orthonormal frame $(\hat{\mathbf e}_1,\hat{\mathbf e}_2,\hat{\mathbf b})$, with $\hat{\mathbf b}$ pointing along the static magnetic field and the first two directions perpendicular to it.

With temporal dependence $e^{-i\omega t}$, where $\omega$ is the wave angular frequency and $t$ is time, this polarization rotates opposite to positive-ion gyromotion. The complementary [left-hand circularly polarized wave electric field](name:left_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field) co-rotates with positive ions. Handedness is defined relative to the static magnetic field, not the wave-propagation direction.

This quantity includes only the right-hand transverse wave contribution; it excludes the parallel wave component and non-wave electric fields. It is local and is not restricted to a beam or ray path. The full complex contribution is distinct from its amplitude representation, which removes the coefficient's complex phase, and from its real and [imaginary quadratures](name:right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_imaginary_part), which separately retain phase-referenced parts of the same phasor.

items.name: perpendicular_fast_ion_pressure
items.description: Pressure of fast ions of one species is the random-motion stress perpendicular to the local magnetic field, summed over all ionic charge states.
items.documentation:
Pressure of fast ions of a specified species is the field-perpendicular component of their gyrotropic pressure tensor, summed over all ionic charge states. It describes the transverse stress of the suprathermal, nonthermal ion population, distinct from its field-parallel stress.

The perpendicular component is defined by the transverse projection of the species pressure tensor:

$$
p_{i,\mathrm{fast},\perp}=\frac{1}{2}\left[\operatorname{tr}\mathbf{P}_{i,\mathrm{fast}}-\hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\mathbf{P}_{i,\mathrm{fast}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}\right]
$$

where $p_{i,\mathrm{fast},\perp}$ is the perpendicular fast-ion pressure of species $i$, $\mathbf{P}_{i,\mathrm{fast}}$ is that species' charge-state-summed fast-ion pressure tensor defined through central velocity moments, $\operatorname{tr}$ denotes the tensor trace, and $\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf B/|\mathbf B|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field $\mathbf B$. The factor one-half averages the stress over the two perpendicular directions.

This quantity applies locally to one ion species. Its charge-state aggregation is a direct additive sum, not a density-weighted mean; the individual contributions are the [charge-state-resolved perpendicular fast-ion pressures](name:perpendicular_fast_ion_charge_state_pressure). It excludes thermal-ion pressure, electron pressure, contributions from other ion species, and bulk-flow momentum flux.

It supplies the specified species' field-perpendicular contribution to the [fast-ion pressure tensor](name:fast_ion_pressure). Summing this quantity over ion species yields the [perpendicular total fast-ion pressure](name:perpendicular_total_fast_ion_pressure), rather than another charge-state average.

items.name: effective_ion_diffusivity
items.description: Effective ion diffusivity is the vector of directional effective Fickian coefficients for particle transport of the ion population summed over all charge states. A positive component corresponds to diffusive ion flux opposite to the total-ion density gradient in the same resolved direction.
items.documentation:
Effective ion diffusivity is the vector of directional effective Fickian coefficients for particle transport of the ion population summed over all charge states. Each component relates the diffusive total-ion particle flux projected along one resolved physical direction to the physical gradient of the total ion number density along that direction.

The component definition is

$$
\Gamma_{i,a}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{i,a}^{\mathrm{eff}}\left(\hat{e}_a \cdot \nabla n_i\right)
$$

where $a$ labels one resolved physical direction, $\hat{e}_a$ is the normalized direction vector, $D_{i,a}^{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the corresponding effective ion diffusivity component, $\Gamma_{i,a}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive total-ion particle flux component, and $n_i$ is the total ion number density. The projection $\hat{e}_a \cdot \nabla n_i$ is the metric-scaled physical gradient along $a$, not a bare derivative with respect to a coordinate label.

The charge-state aggregation is defined through the flux-gradient relation: $n_i$ and $\Gamma_{i,a}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ are sums over all ion charge states before the effective coefficient is formed. Therefore $D_{i,a}^{\mathrm{eff}}$ is not generally a density-weighted mean of [charge-state-resolved ion diffusivities](name:ion_charge_state_diffusivity). The quantity includes only the diffusive, gradient-driven coefficient; it excludes advective or convective particle transport, source terms, and off-diagonal cross-gradient elements of a rank-two tensor. Concrete directional specializations of this effective quantity include [radial effective ion diffusivity](name:radial_effective_ion_diffusivity); related non-effective ion diffusivity is not a specialization of this effective parent.

Sign convention: Positive when the diffusive ion particle flux component is opposite to the total-ion density gradient along the same resolved direction.

items.name: ion_average_temperature
items.description: Temperature of the combined ion population, defined as the number-density-weighted mean over all ion species and states, including all ionic charge states.
items.documentation:
Temperature of the combined ion population characterizes its mean random translational kinetic energy. It is an effective temperature averaged over ion species and states, rather than the temperature of one selected species or state.

The population average is defined by

$$
T_i = \frac{\sum_s\sum_a n_{s,a}T_{s,a}}{\sum_s\sum_a n_{s,a}}
$$

where $T_i$ is the average ion temperature, $s$ labels ion species, $a$ labels the states of each species, $n_{s,a}$ is the number density of that species in that state, and $T_{s,a}$ is its temperature associated with random translational motion.

The sums include all ion species and states, including all ionic charge states, and exclude electrons and neutral particles. The result is a density-weighted mean, not a sum of temperatures or an equally weighted mean of species temperatures. Bulk-flow energy and internal excitation energy are not included in the constituent temperatures.

This averaging combines populations at the specified plasma location; it does not itself perform a spatial average. Spatial averaging, as in [volume-averaged total ion temperature](name:volume_averaged_total_ion_temperature), is a separate operation. Unlike [plasma temperature](name:plasma_temperature), which characterizes the combined charged-particle population, this quantity includes ions alone.

items.name: flux_due_to_pumping
items.description: Inverse-time measure of transport associated with a pumping-induced flux, defined independently of the particular boundary location where the flux is evaluated.
items.documentation:
This quantity represents the rate contribution to plasma transport produced by a pumping process. It characterizes the pumping-associated flux contribution rather than an unrelated transport mechanism.

The parent applies to the transported population represented by the underlying flux and does not prescribe a particular boundary, surface, or spatial location. It denotes the pumping contribution alone, not the total flux obtained by combining pumping with other mechanisms.

[Flux at the wall due to pumping](name:flux_at_wall_due_to_pumping) is a location-specific specialization of this general quantity, evaluated at the wall.

items.name: parallel_counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure
items.description: Parallel pressure is the kinetic-stress component along the magnetic field, including directed-motion stress, carried by suprathermal particles in the counter-passing portion of the distribution. Counter-passing particles move opposite to the plasma-current direction; a flux-surface average aggregates the same component over a magnetic surface.
items.documentation:
Parallel counter-passing fast-particle pressure is the component of kinetic stress along the local magnetic-field direction, carried by suprathermal particles in the counter-passing portion of the distribution. Counter-passing particles move opposite to the plasma-current direction. The uncentered second moment retains stress from directed parallel motion.

The local parallel component is the second velocity moment of the counter-passing fast-particle distribution:

$$
p_{\parallel,\mathrm{cp,fast}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_s \sum_c m_s \int_{\Omega_{\mathrm{cp},s,c}(\mathbf{x})} v_\parallel^2 f_{s,c}^{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

Here $p_{\parallel,\mathrm{cp,fast}}$ is the local parallel counter-passing fast-particle pressure; $s$ labels a fast-particle species; $c$ labels its charge state; $m_s$ is the mass of species $s$; $\mathbf{x}$ is position; $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity; $v_\parallel=\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{b}$ is the velocity component parallel to the local magnetic field; $\mathbf{b}$ is the unit vector along that field; $f_{s,c}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the phase-space number distribution of suprathermal particles of species $s$ and charge state $c$; $\Omega_{\mathrm{cp},s,c}(\mathbf{x})$ is the velocity-space subset for their counter-passing population at $\mathbf{x}$; and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element.

The quantity applies to the suprathermal population and is additively summed over fast-particle species and all charge states, not averaged across them. It excludes thermal particles, co-passing and trapped particles, and stress perpendicular to the magnetic field. The local quantity and its flux-surface average have the same population and parallel-component scope; the average aggregates the local moment over a magnetic surface.

This is the counter-passing contribution to [parallel fast-particle pressure](name:parallel_fast_particle_pressure), which includes parallel stress from other fast-particle orbit classes. Together with the [perpendicular counter-passing fast-particle pressure](name:perpendicular_counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure), it determines the [counter-passing fast-particle pressure](name:counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure), the one-third trace of the kinetic stress for the same population: $p_{\mathrm{cp,fast}}=(p_{\parallel,\mathrm{cp,fast}}+2p_{\perp,\mathrm{cp,fast}})/3$, where $p_{\mathrm{cp,fast}}$ is that scalar pressure and $p_{\perp,\mathrm{cp,fast}}$ is the perpendicular component.

items.name: parallel_net_ion_momentum_source
items.description: Area-normalized net rate of ion momentum transfer along the local magnetic field, summed algebraically over all ionic charge states and contributing source and sink processes.
items.documentation:
The parallel net ion momentum source is the area-normalized net rate of [momentum](name:momentum) transfer to the ion population along the local magnetic field. It retains the sign of the transfer rather than representing its magnitude.

Its defining projection is

$$
S_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{net}} = \hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\mathbf S_i^{\mathrm{net}}
$$

where $S_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{net}}$ is this parallel source, $\mathbf S_i^{\mathrm{net}}$ is the vector [net ion momentum source](name:net_ion_momentum_source), and the subscript $i$ identifies the ion population. The unit vector $\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf B/|\mathbf B|$ points along the local magnetic field $\mathbf B$; the projection is defined where that field is nonzero.

The source is summed over all ionic charge states of the ion population and all contributing physical processes, combining opposing transfers algebraically rather than summing their magnitudes. It excludes the [neutral momentum source](name:neutral_momentum_source), although interactions with neutrals can contribute momentum transfer to ions. It is a source term in the ion momentum balance, not a [momentum flux](name:momentum_flux) describing transport across an oriented surface.

Sign convention: Positive when the net momentum transfer to ions points along the local magnetic field.

items.name: vertical_coordinate_of_constraint_position
items.description: Vertical coordinate of the constraint position specifies its signed height from the zero-height plane, parallel to the symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
Vertical coordinate of the constraint position is its signed height relative to the zero-height plane in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. Here $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis.

The coordinate is defined by

$$
Z = \mathbf{x}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is the position vector of the constraint position measured from the coordinate origin, and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the upward unit vector along the symmetry axis.

This quantity applies individually at each constraint position. It is a point coordinate, not a spatial average of position or the value of the constrained physical observable.

The same vertical projection defines the [vertical coordinate of a measurement position](name:vertical_coordinate_of_measurement_position), while this quantity is specifically evaluated at the constraint position.

Sign convention: Positive when the constraint position lies above the zero-height plane along the upward unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$.

items.name: runaway_electron_source_rate_due_to_compton_scattering
items.description: Compton runaway-electron source rate is the volumetric production of runaway electrons through energy transfer from high-energy gamma-ray photons.
items.documentation:
Compton runaway-electron source rate is the production of runaway electrons per volume and time when high-energy gamma-ray photons transfer sufficient energy to thermal electrons through Compton scattering.

The unaveraged source contribution is defined by

$$
S_{\mathrm C}=\left.\frac{\partial n_{\mathrm{RE}}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{Compton}}
$$

where $S_{\mathrm C}$ is the Compton source rate, $n_{\mathrm{RE}}$ is runaway-electron number density, and $t$ is time. The restricted derivative denotes production attributable to Compton scattering, not the net density change from all processes.

Only electrons entering the runaway population contribute; Compton recoil electrons that remain outside that population are excluded. Other generation mechanisms, transport, and losses are excluded. This source is one additive contribution to the [total runaway-electron source rate](name:total_runaway_electron_source_rate).

The quantity is a volumetric rate, not a volume-integrated production rate. Its [plasma-volume-averaged counterpart](name:volume_averaged_runaway_electron_source_rate_due_to_compton_scattering) is $\overline{S}_{\mathrm C}=V^{-1}\int_V S_{\mathrm C}\,dV$, where $\overline{S}_{\mathrm C}$ denotes that average, $V$ is the plasma volume, and $dV$ is a volume element. Averaging preserves the Compton mechanism and runaway-population restrictions.

items.name: vertical_coordinate_of_magnetic_axis
items.description: Vertical coordinate of the magnetic axis gives its signed height relative to the zero-height plane in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
Vertical coordinate of the magnetic axis is its signed height relative to the zero-height plane in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. Here $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis.

The coordinate is defined by

$$
Z_{\mathrm{axis}} = \mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the magnetic-axis vertical coordinate, $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the position vector of the magnetic-axis location relative to the coordinate origin, and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector in the positive vertical direction along the symmetry axis.

This quantity supplies only the vertical component of the magnetic-axis position, not its major radius, a vertical extent, or a height averaged over the plasma. It is distinct from the [vertical coordinate of the plasma-current center](name:vertical_coordinate_of_current_center), which locates the current-density-weighted centroid, and from the [vertical coordinate of an X-point](name:vertical_coordinate_of_x_point), which refers to a different equilibrium location.

Sign convention: Positive when the magnetic axis lies above the zero-height plane in the positive $Z$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

The closed magnetic-field line about which nested toroidal magnetic flux surfaces are arranged. Where $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{p}}(R_{\mathrm{axis}}, Z_{\mathrm{axis}}) = 0$, $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is poloidal magnetic field; $R_{\mathrm{axis}}, Z_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the O-point inside the nested closed flux surfaces.

items.name: neutral_state_power_density
items.description: Net energy-transfer rate per unit physical volume for neutral particles of a specified species and internal state, entering that population's energy transport equation.
items.documentation:
Neutral-state power density is the net rate at which energy is transferred to or from neutral particles of a specified species and internal state per unit physical volume. It is the source or sink term for that recipient population in its energy transport equation.

The volumetric source term is defined by

$$
p_{s,a} = \left.\frac{\partial u_{s,a}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{sources}} = \sum_r Q_{s,a}^{(r)}
$$

where $p_{s,a}$ is the neutral-state power density, $u_{s,a}$ is the energy density of the selected neutral population, $t$ is time, $s$ identifies the neutral species, $a$ identifies its internal state, $r$ indexes the included energy-transfer processes, and $Q_{s,a}^{(r)}$ is the volumetric energy-transfer contribution from process $r$. The restriction to sources excludes changes arising solely from spatial transport.

The aggregation is a net sum over the included source and loss processes, which can include heating, ionization, and charge exchange. The quantity is resolved by internal state, not summed over states, and is neither stored energy density nor power integrated over a volume. Unlike [ion charge-state power density](name:ion_charge_state_power_density), it selects an internal state of a neutral species rather than an ionic charge state.

Summing these contributions over all internal states of the same neutral species gives [neutral power density](name:neutral_power_density), provided the same energy-transfer channels and spatial averaging convention are used.

Sign convention: Positive when energy is transferred to the selected neutral-state population.

items.name: radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
items.description: Effective kinematic diffusion coefficient for redistribution of the major-radius momentum component carried by ions of one specified species and charge state.
items.documentation:
The radial ion charge-state momentum diffusion coefficient governs diffusive redistribution of the major-radius component of [momentum](name:momentum) carried by ions of one specified species and charge state. The major-radius direction is the direction of increasing $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

In a local kinematic Fick-law closure, the diffusive flux across an oriented surface is:

$$
\Pi_{s,R}^{\rm diff} = -m_s n_s D_{s,R}\,\hat{\mathbf n}\cdot\nabla v_{s,R}
$$

where $s$ identifies the ion species and charge state, $\Pi_{s,R}^{\rm diff}$ is the flux of major-radius momentum across the surface, $m_s$ is the ion mass, $n_s$ is the charge-state number density, $D_{s,R}$ is this diffusion coefficient, $\hat{\mathbf n}$ is the surface's oriented unit normal, $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient operator, and $v_{s,R}$ is the charge-state mean velocity component along increasing major radius.

Radial identifies the transported momentum component, not the direction across which momentum is transported. In particular, the major-radius direction is not generally normal to a magnetic flux surface. The coefficient is charge-state resolved, with no sum or average over charge states implied, and excludes convective momentum transport, nondiffusive residual stress, and external momentum sources.

This quantity specializes the [momentum diffusion coefficient](name:momentum_diffusion_coefficient) to a specified ion charge state and major-radius momentum component. The [parallel ion charge-state momentum diffusion coefficient](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient) is the corresponding specialization for the field-parallel momentum component.

items.name: surface_area_of_optical_element
items.description: Geometric area of the specified optically active material surface of an optical element, measured on the physical surface rather than as its projected aperture.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the geometric area contributed by one specified optically active surface of an optical element. It is a component of the total area of the optical element, not the projected clear-aperture area.

The component area is defined by

$$
A_c = \int_{\mathcal{S}_c} dA
$$

where $\mathcal{S}_c$ is the specified physical material surface and $dA$ is its differential surface-area element. The surface may be curved or planar. Inactive material regions and projected-area representations are excluded; when the active surfaces form a disjoint partition, their component areas sum to the total optical-element area.

items.name: parallel_fast_neutral_pressure
items.description: Pressure of suprathermal neutrals of one species is their normal kinetic stress along the local magnetic field, summed over contributing states rather than averaged.
items.documentation:
Pressure of suprathermal neutrals of a specified species is the field-parallel normal component of their kinetic pressure tensor. It characterizes the stress carried along the local magnetic-field direction by the nonthermal neutral population.

The parallel component is defined by the tensor projection:

$$
p_{0,\parallel}^{\mathrm{fast}} = \hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\mathsf{P}_{0}^{\mathrm{fast}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}
$$

where $p_{0,\parallel}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the parallel fast-neutral pressure, $\mathsf{P}_{0}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the [fast-neutral pressure tensor](name:fast_neutral_pressure), and $\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf B/|\mathbf B|$ is the unit vector along the nonzero local magnetic field $\mathbf B$. The subscript $0$ denotes the neutral species, and the superscript $\mathrm{fast}$ identifies its suprathermal population.

The quantity applies to one neutral species and includes an additive sum over all its internal quantum and excitation states. When multiple charge-state contributions are represented for the species, their pressures are also summed; for strictly neutral particles, only the zero-charge contribution remains. This aggregation is a pressure sum, not a density-weighted mean. It excludes thermal-neutral pressure and pressure from other species, and it is distinct from an internal-state-resolved pressure.

Together with the [perpendicular fast-neutral pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_neutral_pressure), this component specifies the gyrotropic fast-neutral pressure tensor. The parallel component is neither the perpendicular component nor the isotropic trace average; the parallel and perpendicular components coincide for isotropic stress. The magnetic field supplies the projection direction without implying direct magnetic confinement of the neutral particles.

items.name: atomic_mass
items.description: Atomic mass is the mass assigned per atom of a specified elemental or isotopic composition, using a neutral reference atom that includes its bound electrons.
items.documentation:
Atomic mass is the mass assigned to one neutral reference atom of a specified element or isotope, including its bound electrons. It specifies atomic composition independently of the ionic charge state of a species containing that element.

The atomic mass is related to the corresponding relative atomic mass by

$$
m = A_{\mathrm r}\,m_{\mathrm u}
$$

where $m$ is the atomic mass, $A_{\mathrm r}$ is the relative atomic mass, and $m_{\mathrm u}$ is the atomic mass constant, defined as one twelfth of the rest mass of a free neutral carbon-12 atom in its ground state.

The value applies per atom of the selected constituent, not to the total species population or an entire molecule. For a specified isotopic mixture, it denotes the isotope-abundance-weighted mean per atom. It is a physical mass, not the dimensionless relative atomic mass, the integer nucleon count called the mass number, or the charge-dependent rest mass of a particular ion.

Unlike [atomic number](name:atomic_number), which counts nuclear protons and is unchanged across isotopes, atomic mass depends on isotopic composition. [Neutral-beam atomic mass](name:neutral_beam_atomic_mass) specializes this per-atom quantity to the neutral beam species.

items.name: second_local_tangential_width_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
items.description: Full lateral extent of a rectangular electron-cyclotron launcher mirror measured along its designated second local tangential (X2) axis.
items.documentation:
The full width is the edge-to-edge lateral extent of an electron-cyclotron launcher mirror measured along its designated second local tangential (X2) axis. It is defined in the mirror-local tangent frame, not as a machine radial or vertical dimension.

For rectangular mirror geometry, the width is the absolute separation of the opposite edges along the X2 coordinate:

$$
w_2 = \left|x_{2,a} - x_{2,b}\right|
$$

where $w_2$ is the mirror width and $x_{2,a}$ and $x_{2,b}$ are the second local tangential coordinates of the two opposite mirror edges. This is the complete width, not a half-width, curvature, or steering angle; the corresponding orthogonal extent is the [first local tangential width](name:first_local_tangential_width_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror).

Sign convention: Positive when the mirror extent is measured along the designated positive second local tangential axis.

items.name: parallel_fast_electron_pressure
items.description: Pressure of fast electrons parallel to the local magnetic field is the normal stress arising from random field-aligned motion of the suprathermal electron population.
items.documentation:
Pressure of fast electrons parallel to the local magnetic field is the field-aligned normal component of their kinetic pressure tensor. It describes random momentum transport by the nonthermal electron population without imposing pressure isotropy.

The parallel component is defined by projecting the fast-electron pressure tensor along the magnetic-field direction:

$$
p_{e,\mathrm{fast},\parallel}=\hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\mathbf P_{e,\mathrm{fast}}\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}
$$

where $p_{e,\mathrm{fast},\parallel}$ is the parallel fast-electron pressure, $\mathbf P_{e,\mathrm{fast}}$ is the kinetic pressure tensor associated with [fast electron pressure](name:fast_electron_pressure), and $\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf B/|\mathbf B|$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field $\mathbf B$.

The quantity includes the random-motion stress of the fast-electron population only. It excludes thermal-electron pressure, ion pressure, and directed bulk-flow momentum flux. It is a single normal stress, not the isotropic average of the pressure-tensor components.

Together with the [perpendicular fast-electron pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_electron_pressure), it specifies the two independent normal stresses in a gyrotropic description. The perpendicular component is the mean of the two transverse normal stresses; equality of the parallel and perpendicular components gives the isotropic-pressure limit.

items.name: co_passing_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Co-passing thermal electron torque density due to collisions is the local angular-momentum transfer rate per volume delivered to bulk thermal electrons through Coulomb collisions involving co-passing fast particles.
items.documentation:
Co-passing thermal electron torque density due to collisions is the local angular-momentum transfer rate per volume delivered to the bulk thermal electron population through Coulomb collisions involving co-passing fast particles.

Its vector form is related to the collisional momentum-transfer density by

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{co,coll}}(\mathbf{r}) = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{R}_{e,\mathrm{co,coll}}(\mathbf{r})
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{co,coll}}$ is the torque-density vector, $\mathbf{r}$ is the displacement from the chosen torque origin, and $\mathbf{R}_{e,\mathrm{co,coll}}$ is the collisional momentum-transfer density acting on thermal electrons through the co-passing fast-particle channel.

The co-passing restriction applies to the fast-particle distribution; the receiving population remains the bulk thermal electrons. The quantity is independent of component selection: [toroidal co-passing thermal electron torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_co_passing_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions) is its toroidal component, while it is a co-passing specialization of [thermal electron torque density due to collisions](name:thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions). It is distinct from the [toroidal counter-passing thermal electron torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_counter_passing_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

Sign convention: Positive when a component of $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{co,coll}}$ points toward increasing $R$, increasing $\phi$, or increasing $Z$, respectively, in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: parallel_fast_particle_energy
