items.description: Parallel fast-particle energy is the kinetic energy stored in motion along the local magnetic field, integrated over the plasma volume for a specified suprathermal population.
items.documentation:
Parallel fast-particle energy is the global kinetic-energy content associated with motion along the local magnetic field in a specified suprathermal population. It includes particles moving both along and against the field.

For nonrelativistic motion, the defining distribution-function moment is:

$$
W_{\mathrm{fast},\parallel} = \sum_s \int_V d^3x \int d^3v\, \frac{m_s v_\parallel^2}{2}\,f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})
$$

where $W_{\mathrm{fast},\parallel}$ is the parallel fast-particle energy, $s$ labels each species included in the specified fast population, $V$ is the plasma integration volume, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $m_s$ is the particle mass of species $s$. The fast-particle distribution function $f_{s,\mathrm{fast}}$ is normalized so that its velocity integral gives the local fast-particle number density of species $s$. The parallel velocity is $v_\parallel = \mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}$, where $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field.

This quantity sums the parallel kinetic energy of all particles in the specified fast population; it is not a local energy density or an individual particle energy. It excludes the thermal background and perpendicular kinetic energy, without restricting the fast population to ions or to a particular energization mechanism.

For the same population and integration volume, this quantity and the [perpendicular fast-particle energy](name:perpendicular_fast_particle_energy) sum to the total [fast-particle energy](name:fast_particle_energy).

items.name: total_plasma_momentum
items.description: Net linear momentum carried by all plasma species within the confined plasma volume, obtained by integrating their local momentum densities as a vector.
items.documentation:
Total plasma momentum is the vector sum of the linear momenta of all plasma species contained within the confined plasma volume. It is the volume-integrated counterpart of local momentum density, rather than a single-species or direction-specific contribution.

$$
\mathbf{P}_{\mathrm{pl}} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{pl}}} \sum_s \rho_s(\mathbf{x})\,\mathbf{v}_s(\mathbf{x})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $\mathbf{P}_{\mathrm{pl}}$ is the total plasma momentum, $V_{\mathrm{pl}}$ is the confined plasma volume, $\rho_s$ is the mass density of species $s$, and $\mathbf{v}_s$ is its bulk velocity. This is the volume-integrated form of [plasma momentum](name:plasma_momentum). Its all-species toroidal projection is represented by [toroidal total plasma momentum](name:toroidal_total_plasma_momentum).

No directional projection or species weighting beyond the physical mass density is applied; projections are derived from the resulting vector.

Sign convention: Each component is positive when the corresponding momentum component points along the positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ basis.

items.name: fast_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Signed volumetric rate of Coulomb-collisional energy transfer to a fast-particle distribution from ions of one specified species and charge state, including all guiding-center orbit classes.
items.documentation:
Ion-charge-state-resolved fast-particle collisional power density is the signed rate at which Coulomb collisions with a specified ion charge state change the kinetic-energy density of a fast-particle distribution. The charge-state label identifies the collision partner, not the population receiving the power.

For a fast species, this contribution is the kinetic-energy moment of the corresponding Coulomb collision operator:

$$
P_{f\leftarrow i,z}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{x}) = \int \frac{1}{2}m_f |\mathbf{v}|^2 C_{f,i z}(f_f,f_{i,z})(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $P_{f\leftarrow i,z}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the power density received by the fast population, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $m_f$ is the fast-species particle mass, and $f_f$ is its velocity distribution. The indices $i$ and $z$ identify the partner ion species and ionic charge number, $f_{i,z}$ is that partner's velocity distribution, and $C_{f,i z}$ gives the collisional time derivative of $f_f$ due to that partner. The integral covers all velocities, with $d^3v$ denoting the velocity-space volume element.

No sum over partner ion species or charge states is implied. Co-passing, counter-passing, and trapped fast-particle contributions are all included. Orbit-resolved quantities such as [co-passing fast-ion charge-state collisional power density](name:co_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions) isolate an orbit-class exchange; contributions defined as power received by ions must have their signs reversed before combining them using the fast-population recipient convention. Local and flux-surface-averaged forms share this definition, with the latter averaging the entire local collision moment rather than integrating it over a volume.

For energy-conserving Coulomb collisions, the corresponding exchange contribution to [ion charge-state collisional power density](name:ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions) is equal and opposite. This quantity excludes exchanges with other collision partners, ionization and excitation energy changes, and stored kinetic-energy density.

Sign convention: Positive when Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy from the specified ion charge state to the fast-particle distribution; negative when the fast-particle distribution loses kinetic energy to that ion charge state.

items.name: toroidal_co_passing_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Toroidal projection of the collisional angular-momentum source density transferred to co-passing fast electrons.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the signed toroidal component of the local angular-momentum transfer density delivered to co-passing fast electrons by Coulomb collisions. It is the toroidal component of the vector quantity co-passing fast-electron torque density due to collisions.

$$
\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{coll}}^{e,\mathrm{co}} = \hat{\phi} \cdot \boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{e,\mathrm{co}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{coll}}^{e,\mathrm{co}}$ is the collisional torque-density vector transferred to co-passing fast electrons and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The quantity includes Coulomb-collision transfer only and excludes the counter-passing population, which is represented separately by [toroidal counter-passing fast-electron torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_counter_passing_fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

Sign convention: Positive when the transferred angular momentum points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: density_at_pedestal_top
items.description: Local number density of a selected plasma population, including free electrons, ionized species, or an effective fuel species, at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge pedestal.
items.documentation:
Local number density at the H-mode edge pedestal top is the concentration of one selected plasma species or effective pseudo-species at the core-side shoulder of the transport barrier. It is not a sum over different species.

The local number density is defined by

$$
n_s(\mathbf{x}_{\rm pt}) = \lim_{\Delta V \to 0} \frac{\Delta N_s(\mathbf{x}_{\rm pt},\Delta V)}{\Delta V}
$$

where $n_s$ is the local number density of population $s$, $\mathbf{x}_{\rm pt}$ is the position at the pedestal top, $\Delta V$ is a volume surrounding that position, and $\Delta N_s$ is the number of particles of population $s$ within that volume.

For an ion species, the density is the sum $n_s = \sum_z n_{s,z}$ over all represented positive ionic charge states, where $z$ is the ionic charge state and $n_{s,z}$ is the density in that state; neutral atoms are excluded. The electron instance counts free electrons, while the deuterium-tritium instance treats the fuel mixture as one effective pseudo-species. The quantity is local and is not line-, surface-, or volume-averaged. The pedestal-top location is defined by the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal).

Species-specific instances include [hydrogen density at the pedestal top](name:hydrogen_density_at_pedestal_top) and [electron density at the pedestal top](name:electron_density_at_pedestal_top). Unlike [normalized ion species number density](name:normalized_ion_species_number_density), this quantity is an absolute local density rather than a density divided by a reference value, and unlike [fast ion density](name:fast_ion_density), it is not restricted to a fast nonthermal population.

items.name: poloidal_ion_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description: Dimensionless coefficient setting the free-streaming bound on the flux of poloidal momentum carried by one specified ion state in edge plasma.
items.documentation:
This coefficient scales the free-streaming upper bound on the transport flux of the poloidal component of [momentum](name:momentum) carried by one specified ion state in edge plasma. It limits the flux magnitude without reversing its direction.

The limiting flux scale is defined by:

$$
\Pi^{\max}_{s,\mathrm{p}} = \alpha_{s,\mathrm{p}}\Pi^{\mathrm{fs}}_{s,\mathrm{p}}
$$

where $s$ identifies the ion state, $\mathrm{p}$ denotes the poloidal momentum component, $\alpha_{s,\mathrm{p}}$ is this nonnegative limiter coefficient, $\Pi^{\mathrm{fs}}_{s,\mathrm{p}}$ is the nonnegative free-streaming reference flux magnitude, and $\Pi^{\max}_{s,\mathrm{p}}$ is the resulting flux-magnitude bound. Both flux scales refer to transport across the same oriented surface. The coefficient specifies the limiting scale, not a unique interpolation formula for approaching that bound.

Poloidal identifies the transported momentum component, not the direction in which that momentum crosses the surface. The coefficient applies to the selected ion state rather than a sum or average over states; the state may distinguish ionization or another internal state. It is a flux-limiting parameter, not a momentum diffusivity or convection velocity.

This quantity specializes the [momentum flux limiter coefficient](name:momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) by momentum component and ion state. The [poloidal ion charge-state momentum flux limiter coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) explicitly restricts the state identity to an ionic charge state.

items.name: current_of_correction_coil
items.description: Signed conventional current circulating through a non-axisymmetric correction-coil winding and determining its electromagnetic excitation.
items.documentation:
Correction-coil current is the signed rate of charge transport through the winding circuit. It represents the net circuit current driving the magnetic field generated by the correction coil, rather than the local current density within its conductor.

The current is defined by

$$
I = \frac{dQ}{dt}
$$

where $I$ is conventional current, $Q$ is transported electric charge in coulombs, and $t$ is time in seconds. Its electrical behavior is related to the coil's [resistance](name:resistance_of_correction_coil), while the conductor geometry is characterized by its [cross-sectional area](name:area_of_correction_coil). It is distinct from [passive-loop current](name:current_of_passive_loop), which is induced in a passive conducting loop rather than deliberately driven through a correction-coil winding.

Sign convention: Positive when conventional current flows in the designated positive direction around the correction-coil winding; reversing the winding traversal reverses the sign.

items.name: electron_particle_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description: Multiplicative factor that caps electron particle-flux density relative to its collisionless free-streaming bound without reversing the transport direction.
items.documentation:
The electron particle flux limiter coefficient is a multiplicative factor that scales the collisionless free-streaming upper bound on electron particle-flux density in an electron-density transport closure. It limits the permitted magnitude while preserving the direction or sign assigned by the underlying closure.

The permitted electron particle-flux density satisfies:

$$
\left\lVert \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_e \right\rVert \leq L_e\,\Gamma_e^{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_e$ is the limited electron particle-flux density, $L_e$ is the electron particle flux limiter coefficient, and $\Gamma_e^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the nonnegative collisionless free-streaming reference bound supplied by the closure. Nonnegative $L_e$ values below unity impose a stricter cap relative to that reference. The coefficient specifies the cap, not the functional form by which the closure approaches it.

This coefficient applies specifically to electron number transport in the density equation, not to electron energy or momentum transport. It selects no spatial component and is not a coefficient aggregated over plasma species.

It is the electron-specific form of the [particle flux limiter coefficient](name:particle_flux_limiter_coefficient) within the [flux limiter coefficient](name:flux_limiter_coefficient) family. In contrast, the [ion charge-state particle flux limiter coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_particle_flux_limiter_coefficient) limits particle transport for one specified ionic charge state.

items.name: volume_of_flux_surface
items.description: Volume enclosed by a magnetic flux surface, accumulated over its full interior rather than only the shell between adjacent surfaces.
items.documentation:
Volume of flux surface

The volume is defined by

$$
V = \int_{\Omega} d^3\mathbf{x}
$$

where $V$ is the enclosed volume, $\Omega$ is the spatial domain inside the selected magnetic flux surface, $\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position, and $d^3\mathbf{x}$ is the differential volume element.

The integral covers the entire enclosed region and excludes space outside the selected surface. It is not a local shell volume; differences between enclosed volumes give the volume between neighboring surfaces. For successively enclosing nested surfaces, the volume increases from zero at the magnetic axis.

When the selected surface coincides with the plasma boundary, this quantity equals the [volume enclosed by the plasma boundary](name:volume_of_plasma_boundary). The [poloidal-flux derivative](name:derivative_of_volume_of_flux_surface_with_respect_to_poloidal_magnetic_flux_coordinate) and [toroidal-flux derivative](name:derivative_of_volume_of_flux_surface_with_respect_to_toroidal_flux_coordinate) describe its rate of change with their respective flux coordinates and provide the geometric measures relating flux-coordinate intervals to enclosed shell volumes.

A surface formed by points sharing the same magnetic-flux label in a nested-flux-surface configuration. Where $\psi(R, Z) = \mathrm{const}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux.

items.name: thermal_electron_energy
items.description: Volume-integrated thermal energy content of the electron population, excluding fast suprathermal electrons and non-electron plasma populations.
items.documentation:
Volume-integrated thermal energy content of the electron population is the total kinetic energy carried by bulk thermal electrons throughout the confined plasma. It is an extensive energy content, not a power or energy-transfer rate, and excludes fast suprathermal electrons and non-electron populations.

The defining relation is

$$
E_{e,\mathrm{th}} = \frac{3}{2}\int_{V_\mathrm{plasma}} p_{e,\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $E_{e,\mathrm{th}}$ is the integrated thermal electron energy, $p_{e,\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local thermal electron pressure, $V_\mathrm{plasma}$ is the confined plasma volume, and $\mathbf{r}$ denotes position. This quantity is the thermal-electron component of [electron energy](name:volume_integrated_square_of_poloidal_magnetic_field); unlike [thermal plasma energy](name:thermal_plasma_energy), it excludes thermal-ion energy.

items.name: diamagnetic_momentum_diffusivity
items.description: Effective kinematic coefficient for down-gradient diffusion of the diamagnetic momentum component of a selected plasma or neutral population.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the effective kinematic coefficient governing diffusion of the diamagnetic component of [momentum](name:momentum). It specializes [momentum diffusivity](name:momentum_diffusivity) by the transported momentum component, without fixing the direction in which that momentum crosses a surface.

Within a local Fick-law closure, the defining relation is:

$$
\Pi_{\mathrm{dia}}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -\chi_{\mathrm{dia}}\,\hat{\mathbf n}\cdot\nabla g_{\mathrm{dia}}
$$

where $\Pi_{\mathrm{dia}}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive flux of diamagnetic momentum across an oriented surface, $\chi_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is this diffusivity, $\hat{\mathbf n}$ is the surface unit normal, $g_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the local diamagnetic momentum density of the selected population, and $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient operator.

The coefficient applies to aggregate plasma momentum, ion or neutral species, or a resolved charge or internal state. Examples include [charge-state-resolved ion diffusivity](name:ion_charge_state_diamagnetic_momentum_diffusivity) and [neutral-species diffusivity](name:neutral_diamagnetic_momentum_diffusivity). Aggregate momentum densities are summed over their included constituents, and species-level ion momentum is summed over all charge states; resolved-state forms include only the specified state. An aggregate diffusivity relates the aggregate diffusive flux to its momentum-density gradient and is not a sum of constituent diffusivities.

The closure acts on the momentum-density gradient, not directly on the velocity gradient. It excludes advective transport, represented separately by [diamagnetic momentum convection velocity](name:diamagnetic_momentum_convection_velocity), as well as residual stress and external momentum sources. The diamagnetic label identifies the momentum component in the closure; it does not by itself specify a drift-driven diffusion mechanism or imply charged-particle drift motion for neutrals.

items.name: radial_neutral_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description: Dimensionless coefficient scaling the free-streaming cap on flux of cylindrical radial momentum carried by one neutral species in a specified internal state in edge-plasma transport.
items.documentation:
This coefficient scales the collisionless free-streaming upper bound on the magnitude of the modeled flux of cylindrical radial [momentum](name:momentum) carried by one neutral species in a specified internal state. Limiting constrains the flux magnitude without reversing its direction.

The upper bound is defined by:

$$
\Pi_{s,R}^{\max} = \alpha_{s,R}\,\Pi_{s,R}^{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $\Pi_{s,R}^{\max}$ is the permitted flux-magnitude bound, $\alpha_{s,R}$ is this limiter coefficient, and $\Pi_{s,R}^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the reference free-streaming flux magnitude across the same oriented surface. The label $s$ identifies the neutral species and internal state, and the subscript $R$ identifies the transported radial momentum component. The free-streaming reference and the function enforcing this bound are closure-dependent.

Radial means the direction of increasing major radius in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It identifies the momentum component being transported, not the transport direction across the surface. In particular, it does not imply flux-surface-normal transport.

This quantity specializes the [momentum flux limiter coefficient](name:momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) to a single neutral species, internal state, and momentum component; it is not summed or averaged over species or internal states. It is a bound-scaling coefficient, not the momentum flux itself or a momentum diffusivity. The [vertical neutral momentum flux limiter coefficient](name:vertical_neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient) instead applies to the vertical momentum component.

items.name: accumulated_total_gas_count_at_midplane_due_to_gas_injection
items.description: Accumulated total gas count at midplane due to gas injection is the cumulative unweighted count of neutral gas particles introduced by all injection valves near the equatorial midplane over the specified accumulation interval. It sums all injected species and is not weighted by neutral electron count, atomic number, mass, or valve identity.
items.documentation:
Accumulated total gas count at midplane due to gas injection is the cumulative unweighted count of neutral gas particles introduced by all gas-injection valves assigned to the equatorial-midplane valve group. It aggregates all injected species and all valves in that group; each gas particle contributes one count to the total inventory.

The accumulation over a specified time interval is the time integral of the unweighted total midplane gas-particle source rate:

$$
N_{\mathrm{gas,mid}}(t_1;t_0) = \int_{t_0}^{t_1} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{gas,mid}}(t')\,dt'
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{gas,mid}}$ is the accumulated dimensionless count, $t_0$ and $t_1$ are the interval endpoints in seconds, $t'$ is the integration time in seconds, and $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{gas,mid}}$ is the [total gas source rate at midplane due to gas injection](name:total_gas_source_rate_at_midplane_due_to_gas_injection) in particles per second, summed over all midplane gas-injection valves and all injected species.

For a post-breakdown accumulated inventory, $t_0$ is the plasma-breakdown time; for a prefill inventory, the interval is the pre-breakdown gas-fill interval. This quantity is the midplane contribution to the all-position [accumulated total particle count due to gas injection], not a per-valve count and not an equivalent-electron inventory. Species-specific inventories such as accumulated neon count due to gas injection, [accumulated nitrogen count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_nitrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection), and [accumulated carbon count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_carbon_count_due_to_gas_injection) are separate components of the injected species inventory.

items.name: vertical_coordinate_of_strike_point
items.description: Vertical coordinate of a selected divertor strike point, specifying its signed height relative to the coordinate origin in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
Vertical coordinate of a selected divertor strike point specifies its signed height relative to the coordinate origin in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The coordinate is defined by

$$
Z = \mathbf{x}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $Z$ is the strike-point vertical coordinate, $\mathbf{x}$ is the position vector from the coordinate origin to that strike point, and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis and oriented toward increasing $Z$. The other cylindrical coordinates are $R$, the major radius, and $\phi$, the toroidal angle.

Each value refers to one selected strike point, including separately identified inner and outer strike points, rather than an average over multiple strike points. It uses the same vertical projection as the [vertical coordinate of an X-point](name:vertical_coordinate_of_x_point), but refers to a different location. It is not the [vertical coordinate of the divertor-target geometric center](name:z_coordinate_of_divertor_target).

Sign convention: Positive when the strike-point displacement from the coordinate origin has a positive projection onto $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$.

The point where a divertor separatrix branch intersects a plasma-facing target. Where $\psi(R_{\mathrm{s}}, Z_{\mathrm{s}}) = \psi_{\mathrm{X}}$, $R_{\mathrm{s}}, Z_{\mathrm{s}}$ is the point on the target surface; $\psi_{\mathrm{X}}$ is poloidal magnetic flux at the primary X-point.

items.name: perpendicular_wave_vector_magnitude
items.description: Non-negative magnitude of the wave vector transverse to the local equilibrium magnetic field, setting the inverse cross-field phase scale.
items.documentation:
The perpendicular wave-vector magnitude is the non-negative length of the part of a local electromagnetic wave vector transverse to the equilibrium magnetic field. It characterizes cross-field phase variation and is the scalar magnitude associated with the perpendicular wave vector.

For wave vector $\mathbf{k}$ and magnetic-field unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$, the perpendicular magnitude is defined by

$$
k_\perp = \left|\mathbf{k} - (\mathbf{k}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}})\hat{\mathbf{b}}\right|
$$

where $k_\perp$ and $\mathbf{k}$ have units of inverse length, and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is tangent to the local equilibrium magnetic-field direction. The quantity excludes the wave-vector component parallel to the magnetic field and is non-negative by definition.

items.name: fluctuating_ion_current_density
items.description: Ion current density is the vector density of conventional electric charge flux carried by ions, obtained by charge-weighting their directed particle motion across unit area.
items.documentation:
Ion current density $\mathbf{J}_i$ is the vector density of conventional electric charge flux carried by ions. It represents signed charge transport from all included ion species and charge states.

The kinetic definition is the charge-weighted first velocity moment of the ion distribution functions:

$$
\mathbf{J}_i(\mathbf{x},t) = \sum_{s\in\mathrm{ions}} q_s \int \mathbf{v}\,f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v = \sum_{s\in\mathrm{ions}} q_s n_s \mathbf{u}_s
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $t$ is time, $s$ indexes ion species and charge states, $q_s$ is the charge of population $s$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_s$ is its velocity-space distribution function, $n_s$ is its number density, and $\mathbf{u}_s$ is its mean velocity.

This quantity includes ion-carried charge flux and excludes electron-carried and displacement-current density. Qualified instances may select a directional projection such as [parallel ion current density](name:parallel_ion_current_density), a collection regime such as [saturated ion current density](name:saturated_ion_current_density), or a fluctuation statistic such as [parallel fluctuating ion current density](name:parallel_fluctuating_ion_current_density).

Sign convention: Positive when an ion-carried charge-flux component is aligned with the positive direction of its defining basis vector or oriented surface normal.

items.name: binormal_wave_electric_field
items.description: Complex phasor of the wave electric field projected onto the local binormal direction, perpendicular to the static magnetic field and tangent to the magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
The binormal wave electric field is the complex phasor obtained by projecting the electromagnetic-wave electric-field phasor onto the local binormal direction, which is perpendicular to the static magnetic field and tangent to the magnetic flux surface. It retains the amplitude and phase of that component and is one component of the [wave electric field](name:wave_electric_field), alongside the [normal wave electric field](name:normal_wave_electric_field).

$$
\widetilde{E}_{\mathrm{bi}}(\mathbf{r},\omega)=\widetilde{\mathbf{E}}_{\mathrm{wave}}(\mathbf{r},\omega)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{bi}}(\mathbf{r})
$$

where $\widetilde{E}_{\mathrm{bi}}$ is the complex binormal electric-field phasor, $\widetilde{\mathbf{E}}_{\mathrm{wave}}$ is the complex wave-electric-field phasor, $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{bi}}$ is the local binormal unit vector, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $\omega$ is angular frequency. The binormal projection is distinct from the [parallel wave electric field](name:parallel_wave_electric_field) and the flux-surface-normal projection.

items.name: ion_charge_state_density
items.description: Number density of ions of a specified species and charge state, including thermal and nonthermal populations without summing over other charge states.
items.documentation:
Number density of ion charge state

The density is the zeroth velocity-space moment of the complete distribution and decomposes into thermal and fast contributions:

$$
n_{s,q} = \int f_{s,q}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v = n_{s,q}^{\mathrm{th}} + n_{s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}}
$$

where $s$ labels the ion species, $q$ is its positive ionic charge number, $n_{s,q}$ is the total number density of that species and charge state, $f_{s,q}$ is its velocity distribution, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The contributions $n_{s,q}^{\mathrm{th}}$ and $n_{s,q}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ are the [thermal ion charge-state number density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_number_density) and [fast ion charge-state density](name:fast_ion_charge_state_density), respectively.

The aggregation includes both particle populations within the specified charge state; it does not sum over different charge states or species. Neutral particles are excluded. The fast contribution is only the nonthermal component, not the complete charge-state population.

Summing this quantity over all positive charge states gives the [total ion number density](name:total_ion_number_density) of the selected species: $n_s = \sum_{q>0} n_{s,q}$, where $n_s$ denotes that charge-state-summed species density.
